source_issues.title: Memorization and generalization overstatements
source_issues.detail: Any dataset, zero test accuracy, always worse for larger models, and no regularization means mere regurgitation are source simplifications. A gap alone does not uniquely establish learned noise, and inconsistent identical inputs cannot all be memorized by a deterministic predictor. Historical GPT-3 corpus/parameter assertions and paper details were not externally verified.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Normalization performance claims are not universal
source_issues.detail: Flatter minima, same accuracy, 10% faster/less overhead, LLM preferences and guaranteed learning-rate stability depend on model/task/hardware. The source treats overhead reduction and speedup interchangeably. No benchmark reproduced or current product claim verified.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Half of neurons is an expectation
source_issues.detail: Independent Bernoulli(.5) masks do not force exactly half each pass; fixed seed 5 kept all four in the finite fixture. Translation correctly preserves the source statement.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Dropout ensemble interpretation is approximate
source_issues.detail: For nonlinear networks, deterministic scaling at inference is not generally exact averaging of all 2^N predictions. Finite training does not literally train every subnetwork on its own minibatch.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Default rates and gap thresholds are heuristic
source_issues.detail: Dropout/weight-decay rates, all-Adam-always-AdamW recommendation, >32 batch cutoff and accuracy-gap thresholds are prescriptive source heuristics, not universal defaults or a measured diagnosis. Percentage versus percentage-point wording is retained.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: L2 and weight-decay distinctions
source_issues.detail: Plain SGD equivalence assumes the same learning-rate scaling and update convention. The table says subtract lambda*w without an explicit learning rate. Small weights do not guarantee generalization, and the network decays weights but not biases. Formula payload and source wording remain unchanged.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Affine normalization and statistic conventions
source_issues.detail: Gamma/beta can restore a chosen scale/shift but cannot universally undo changing batch-dependent normalization. Epsilon makes unit variance approximate. The implementation averages variances, not standard deviations, despite prose referring to sigma.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: BatchNorm explanation is overstated
source_issues.detail: The source calls one explanation wrong and presents smoothing/Lipschitz changes as the actual universal reason despite acknowledging debate. This review did not independently check the cited paper or generality of those claims.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Batch-size limitation depends on normalized axes
source_issues.detail: The one-sample dense fixture collapses normalized activations to zero before affine parameters. Batch size 1 is not generally meaningless when spatial/time axes supply observations; <32 is not a mathematical threshold. Mermaid claims were preserved.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: LayerNorm placement and Transformer example scope
source_issues.detail: Sample-wise normalization and Pre/Post-LN roles are translated correctly. The PyTorch example is Post-LN with default sequence-first MultiheadAttention and no causal/padding masks; it is not a complete causal LM block.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: RMSNorm formula omits stabilizing epsilon
source_issues.detail: Displayed formula divides by RMS without epsilon, whereas documentary code adds eps before sqrt and handles a zero vector. It also has no beta parameter, so shorthand LayerNorm-minus-mean is incomplete. No source correction applied.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Augmentation requires task-specific label invariance
source_issues.detail: Flips, crops, synonym replacement, deletion and pitch shifts can change labels. Seeing one or fifty views does not guarantee memorization or invariant learning; source assertions are faithfully retained.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Early stopping uses validation but exercise reuses test
source_issues.detail: A rising validation loss does not establish an exact not-yet-overfit boundary. Exercise 4 explicitly selects using test loss/accuracy, which contaminates a final held-out evaluation; translation correctly does not silently replace test with validation.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Dropout object has state and validation gaps
source_issues.detail: Local training forward/backward mask and inverted scaling work in the finite fixture. Eval forward leaves a stale mask; eval-first backward raises TypeError. p, lengths and calling order are not validated; zip can silently truncate gradients.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Normalization snippets are forward-only
source_issues.detail: BatchNorm, LayerNorm and RMSNorm define no backward method or gamma/beta updates. Empty inputs can divide by zero; feature count and eps are not validated. Exercise 5 needs additional backward implementations before its training/gradient comparison can run.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Network omits Dropout derivative on hidden path
source_issues.detail: RegularizedNetwork.backward never calls Dropout.backward and omits both zero mask and 1/(1-p) for hidden gradients. With fixed mask [0,1], six hidden weight/bias gradients disagree with independent central differences; no-Dropout all nine parameters agree. Source code copied unchanged.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Training and test accuracy use different measurement conditions
source_issues.detail: Training accuracy aggregates online, changing-weight, dropout-active predictions; test accuracy uses final current weights without dropout. The reported gap therefore is not solely a same-model generalization gap. Fixed example order and global random.seed side effects further limit comparisons.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation

source_issues.title: Sigmoid/BCE clipping and empty evaluation boundaries
source_issues.detail: sigmoid(500) rounds to exactly 1, giving a zero out*(1-out) derivative while clipped BCE may still be large. Empty train/test data divides by zero. The finite fixture is not an exhaustive numerical-stability validation.
source_issues.policy: Preserve fixed-source content; do not repair via translation
